questions.q: What did TerKeurst's therapist point out about her relentless positivity?
a: She was using it to hide her real feelings
It was helping her heal faster than expected
It made her husband more willing to apologize
It had no effect on her either way
questions.why: The first lesson says her therapist saw through the positivity and hyper-spiritual language she used to avoid the pain.

questions.q: What does collecting the dots involve?
a: Looking back at past experiences that shaped your present views
Writing a list of people you still need to apologize to
Tracking your mood every day for a month
Asking friends to describe what you were like as a child
questions.why: The second lesson describes revisiting old memories, such as her absent father and the babysitter's abuse, to see their effect.

questions.q: What did TerKeurst realize she would have to do in order to forgive her husband?
a: Forgive the other men who had betrayed her as well
Give up her career to focus on the marriage
Move away from the town where she grew up
Confront the babysitter from her childhood
questions.why: Connecting the dots showed her that forgiving Art meant also forgiving the men who had betrayed her trust before him.

questions.q: What does correcting the dots mean?
a: Examining beliefs from your past and making sure they are positive
Apologizing for the mistakes you made in past relationships
Replacing painful memories with happier invented ones
Setting strict rules for how future relationships should work
questions.why: The second lesson describes reframing old triggers, reading scripture and asking what a healthy version of herself would do.

questions.q: When painful memories resurface, what does TerKeurst recommend?
a: Name the triggered feeling and decide how to handle it
Push the memory out of your mind as quickly as possible
Call the person who caused it right away
Stop journaling until you feel completely stable
questions.why: The third lesson says she lets herself grieve briefly, then judges whether to talk to the person or write it out.
